title: Pullback of the sheaf associated to a module along a morphism of affine schemes
statement:
Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $\psi=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ the induced morphism of affine schemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For an $R$-module $M$ let $\widetilde M$ and $\tau:M\to\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\widetilde M)$ be as in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] (and likewise for $S$-modules on $\operatorname{Spec}S$), and let $\psi^*$ be the pullback of modules [def-pc-module-pullback], left adjoint to $\psi_*$, with unit $\eta:\mathcal G\to\psi_*\psi^*\mathcal G$. Then there is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}S}$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] $\theta_M:\psi^*\widetilde M\xrightarrow{\sim}\widetilde{S\otimes_RM}$, natural in $M$, such that for every $m\in M$
$$\theta_M\bigl(\eta_{\widetilde M}(\tau(m))\bigr)=\tau(1\otimes m)\quad\text{in }\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}S,\widetilde{S\otimes_RM}),$$
where $\eta_{\widetilde M}(\tau(m))\in(\psi_*\psi^*\widetilde M)(\operatorname{Spec}R)=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}S,\psi^*\widetilde M)$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback), part (1); its proof uses Schemes Lemma 01I7 (lemma-compare-constructions) and Modules Lemma 01BJ (lemma-restrict-quasi-coherent)

proof.text: Identify $R=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal O)$ and $S=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}S,\mathcal O)$, with the homomorphism on sections induced by $\psi$ equal to $\varphi$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](1) (Schemes 01I7), the $R$-module $M$ determines the associated module sheaf $\mathcal F_M$, canonically and naturally isomorphic to $\widetilde M$; this isomorphism carries the canonical section of $m$ to $\tau(m)$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I7 (lemma-compare-constructions), statement and proof; Lemma 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback), first sentence of proof

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-associated-module-pullback] (Modules 01BJ) to the ringed-space morphism $\psi$, the $R$-module $M$, and the isomorphism of Step 1. It gives a canonical isomorphism $\psi^*\widetilde M\cong\mathcal F_{S\otimes_R M}$, functorial in $M$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](1) over $S$ identifies $\mathcal F_{S\otimes_R M}$ with $\widetilde{S\otimes_R M}$; compose these two isomorphisms to define $\theta_M$. Both component isomorphisms are natural, so $\theta_M$ is natural.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01I9 (lemma-widetilde-pullback), proof of (1), citing Schemes 01I7 and Modules 01BJ

proof.text: The isomorphism from Modules 01BJ is the canonical pullback comparison: its construction presents the associated sheaf $\mathcal F_M$ as the pullback of $M$ from the one-point ringed space $(\{*\},R)$, and uses the composition isomorphism of pullbacks. Hence the image of the pullback-unit section $\eta_{\widetilde M}(\tau(m))$ in the associated sheaf for $S\otimes_R M$ is the canonical section belonging to $1\otimes m$: the ring map $R\to S$ sends the scalar $1$ to $1$ and extension of scalars sends $m$ to $1\otimes m$. Under the comparison of Step 2 with $\widetilde{S\otimes_R M}$, this canonical section is $\tau(1\otimes m)$, establishing the required equality. This is the unit compatibility implicit in the canonical construction of Modules 01BJ; it is stated here because the cited Stacks proof only states the isomorphism.
